display.name: GitLab
display.blurb: Browse projects, open merge requests and issues, and inspect pipelines — driven by the official `glab` CLI and authenticated with a brokered personal access token.

cli.doc:
Use `glab` (the official GitLab CLI) to drive GitLab from this session — browse projects, open and review merge requests and issues, and inspect CI/CD pipelines on gitlab.com. Authentication is automatic: the egress proxy injects a capability-scoped GitLab personal access token (Authorization: Bearer) on every request to the GitLab REST API (/api/v4) and strips anything you supply. `GITLAB_TOKEN` is a managed placeholder. Do NOT run `glab auth login` or set a real token.

Common commands and the power each needs:
- Projects: `glab repo view <group/project>`, `glab repo list` — requires `projects:read`.
- Merge requests: `glab mr list`, `glab mr view <id>` (requires `merge_requests:read`); `glab mr create --source-branch <b> --target-branch main --title "..." --description "..."` (requires `merge_requests:write`). To open an MR: push your branch first (git auth is brokered, nothing to configure), then create the MR.
- Issues: `glab issue list`, `glab issue view <iid>` (requires `issues:read`); `glab issue create --title "..." --description "..."` (requires `issues:write`).
- Pipelines: `glab ci list`, `glab ci status`, `glab ci view` (requires `pipelines:read`); `glab ci run`/`glab ci trigger` (requires `pipelines:write`).
- Repository contents (files, tree, commits, branches, tags): read requires `repository:read`; creating commits via the API requires `repository:write`.

Raw REST passthrough: `glab api projects/:id/merge_requests` (GET) or `glab api --method POST projects/:id/issues -f title="..."`. Only the resource families your profile granted are reachable — a call to a path you weren't granted is denied at the network boundary, not authenticated. Run `glab --help` to explore.
